reading.body:
Kentucky's tracked 2026 bills include a dedicated artificial intelligence act, HB455, filed with an emergency declaration, alongside narrower AI adjacent measures on mental health chatbots, algorithmic rent setting, automated license plate readers, and property rights in a person's name, voice, and likeness.

Three separate data privacy bills, HB633, HB559, and HB33, appear in the same session, suggesting either competing legislative approaches to privacy regulation or incremental amendments building on each other, though the data given does not clarify which.

Most of the remaining bills, state budget appropriations, campaign finance, and elections measures, are general governance matters that happen to appear in this AI tracked list without addressing AI directly, illustrating how broad legislative tracking captures far more than AI specific policy.

The data does not indicate which of these 21 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so Kentucky's actual enacted AI framework is not established by this record.
